steps.what: Compare scanned postage with the amount required for processing.
Check items to ensure addresses are legible, correct, and in suitable condition.
Check that sufficient postage or the appropriate documentation is attached.

tasks.design: Where a scan already exists, {OPS_SYSTEM} compares the postage with the tariff amount required for processing. The mail sorter still checks that addresses are legible and correct and that the item is in suitable condition. Sufficient postage or the appropriate documentation is checked by eye when the scan is missing. The compare does not look at the piece.
tasks.previous_blocker: Postage, legibility, and condition were all judged by eye, including amounts a scan had already read.
tasks.enabler_now: A scan that already exists can be compared with the tariff. The piece is still looked at.
tasks.still_hard: A smudged address or a torn wrapper is seen by the sorter, not by a postage figure.
tasks.human_edge: The sorter accepts or rejects the piece. A tariff compare only covers a scanned amount.
tasks.altitude: The look at the piece stays with the sorter. Only a postage figure that was already scanned is compared.

reach.role: Weighers, Measurers, Checkers, and Samplers, Recordkeeping
reach.task: Check a physical item against a stated figure.
reach.learn: A figure is not the condition of the item.

evidence.claim: A postage amount already scanned can be compared with a tariff the organisation holds. The comparison does not read the letter.
Legibility, attached documents, and the condition of the piece are still checked by the sorter.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A mail sorter on the floor of a mid-size European organisation. A code on a screen does not pick up, sort, or rewrap a piece of mail.
Fields: A scan id and a tariff id are required for the compare. With no scan, the sorter checks postage by eye. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the mail sorter finishes it by hand.
Native check: The compare uses the scanned amount only. It does not decide that the address is legible.
unknowns: What share of items have a postage scan before they reach this sorter.
research_questions: Which items are still accepted with no scan and only a visual check?

already_counted.description: Checking the piece and the postage that was not scanned stay with the sorter.

incremental.description: Check the tariff used is the one for this class of mail.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes most items have no scan, so the sorter checks postage by eye and little is saved. High assumes scanned amounts compare cleanly. Looking at the piece is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Print a label depending on destinations already on the sorted tray.
Bundle and label sorted mail for the designated areas.
Route those bundles according to established procedures and deadlines.

tasks.design: A label is printed from {OPS_SYSTEM} only when the sorted tray already has a destination. The mail sorter bundles and labels the mail for the designated areas, then routes the bundles according to the established procedures and deadlines. A tray with no destination id gets no label. The printer does not bundle or carry the mail.
tasks.previous_blocker: Labels were written by hand from a destination the sorter read off the tray.
tasks.enabler_now: A destination already on the tray can be printed. The sorter still makes the bundle and moves it.
tasks.still_hard: A deadline and a full dock are handled by the sorter, not by the label.
tasks.human_edge: The sorter bundles, labels, and routes the mail. The label only repeats the destination.
tasks.altitude: Bundling and routing stay with the sorter. The label is the destination the tray already had.

reach.task: Take a labelled bundle to the right desk.
reach.learn: A printed destination is not the carrying.

evidence.claim: A label can be printed from a destination already stored on the tray. It cannot bundle the mail.
Routing to a designated area by the deadline stays with the sorter.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A mail sorter on the floor of a mid-size European organisation. A code on a screen does not pick up, sort, or rewrap a piece of mail.
Fields: A tray id and a destination id are required. With no destination, no label is printed. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the mail sorter finishes it by hand.
Native check: The label copies the stored destination. It does not choose a new one.
unknowns: Whether every sorted tray has a destination id before it reaches bundling.
research_questions: Which trays are still hand-labelled because the destination was never stored?

already_counted.description: Bundling, labelling, and routing the mail stay with the sorter.

incremental.description: Check the printed destination is the one on the tray.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes trays have no destination id, so the sorter writes labels by hand. High assumes the label prints and the sorter still bundles and routes. The carrying is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the dock location for these mail containers.
Move containers of mail, using equipment such as forklifts or automated trains.
Confirm the containers reached the named location.

tasks.design: The dock location for the containers is shown from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The mail sorter moves the containers using equipment such as forklifts or automated trains, and confirms they reached that location. A container with no location id is moved from the instruction the sorter already has. The screen does not drive the forklift.
tasks.previous_blocker: The dock slot was shouted or written on the container.
tasks.enabler_now: A stored location can be shown before the sorter moves the container.
tasks.still_hard: Driving the forklift or sending the train, and stacking safely, are physical.
tasks.human_edge: The sorter moves the container. A location on a screen is not the move.
tasks.altitude: Moving containers stays with the sorter. The screen only shows a location already stored.

reach.task: Move a load to a named door.
reach.learn: A named door is not the driving.

evidence.claim: A dock location already stored can be shown. It cannot drive a forklift or an automated train.
The sorter confirms arrival. A shown location is not that confirmation.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A mail sorter on the floor of a mid-size European organisation. A code on a screen does not pick up, sort, or rewrap a piece of mail.

Fields: A container id is required before a location is shown. With no id, the sorter uses the instruction they have. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the mail sorter finishes it by hand.
Native check: The sorter operates the forklift or the train. The screen does not.
unknowns: Whether automated trains on this floor are driven by the sorter or run on a fixed path.
research_questions: Which containers leave without a stored dock location?

already_counted.description: Moving the containers and confirming arrival stay with the sorter.

incremental.description: Check the location is the dock for this container.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes containers have no location id, so the sorter moves them as today. High assumes the dock is shown. Driving and lifting are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Print the container label from the route already assigned.
Set aside a container that will not open.

tasks.design: A container label is printed from {OPS_SYSTEM} only when a route is already assigned. The mail sorter opens and labels the mail containers, and sets aside a container that will not open. A container with no route id is not printed. The printer does not open the container.
tasks.previous_blocker: Labels were handwritten, and a stuck container was discovered only when the sorter pulled it.
tasks.enabler_now: An assigned route can be printed. Opening the container stays with the sorter.
tasks.still_hard: A strapped or damaged container is opened by hand, or set aside.
tasks.human_edge: The sorter opens the container and decides it will not open. The label only repeats the route.
tasks.altitude: Opening and labelling stay with the sorter. The label is the route already assigned.

reach.task: Label an item for the next hand-off.
reach.learn: A printed route is not the opening of the container.

evidence.claim: A label can be printed from a route already assigned to the container. It cannot open the container.
A container that will not open is set aside by the sorter.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A mail sorter on the floor of a mid-size European organisation. A code on a screen does not pick up, sort, or rewrap a piece of mail.
Fields: A container id and a route id are required. With no route, no label is printed. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the mail sorter finishes it by hand.
Native check: The sorter opens the container. The label copies the stored route and does not choose one.
unknowns: Whether containers arrive with a route already assigned or only with a handwritten tag.
research_questions: Which containers are still opened with no route id on the record?

already_counted.description: Opening, labelling, and setting aside stuck containers stay with the sorter.

incremental.description: Check the printed route is the one assigned to this container.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low assumes containers have no route id, so the sorter writes the label by hand. High assumes the label prints. Opening the container is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The mail sorter still looks at each item, still bundles and moves the mail, and still opens the containers. A postage figure can be compared when a scan already exists. A label can be printed from a destination the tray already has. The lifting stays.
reach: Couriers and messengers match a label to a destination, and this job learns a printed label is not the bundle.
Weighers, measurers, checkers, and samplers check a physical item, and this job learns a postage compare is not a look at the condition.
skills_to_grow: Look at legibility and condition even when a postage figure is already scanned.
Bundle and move the mail after a label is printed.
Open a container by hand, including one that sticks.
role.ambitious_version: A tray leaves the station with a label taken from its destination, and every item that looks wrong is still pulled by the sorter.
